To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the award of long-term contracts to football players in the German Bundesliga is a positive signal of the quality of players and that this positive signal is associated with a higher probability of winning a match.
(i) the length of a player's contract is a good predictor of his performance on the pitch and (ii) this relationship is not driven by moral hazard effects, but by selection effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economics of long term contracts and their impact on the productivity of footballers in the Bundesliga.
how football clubs manage player contracts in a competitive context.
the economic implications of the long term nature of football contracts in the context of the modern game and the implications for the economics of the football labour market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economics of long term contracts in the Bundesliga is a story of selection, rather than shirking.
, in the German Bundesliga, players with long term contracts are more talented and work harder than players with shorter term contracts.
, in a competitive environment, clubs are willing to invest in the long term development of players, and that this investment is rewarded by better performances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the economics of long term contracts in the footballers’ labour market is not about the risk of players shirking.
long term contracts are used by football clubs as a means of securing talent in the face of rising wages and increasing competition.
, in the context of the German Bundesliga, long term contracts are a useful tool for clubs to manage their labour costs and player talent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long term contracts are a necessary feature of a competitive football league and that the use of short term contracts is likely to be associated with lower performance on the football pitch.
the long term contract is a useful tool for clubs to manage the labour market for footballers and to ensure that they get the most out of the players that they sign.
the economics of long term contracts in football is not the same as in the labour economics literature.
